title: Run Now performs jobs.json writes and per-host Vault credential resolution synchronously on the UI thread
existing_state: The Run Now click path never leaves the UI thread until deep inside execution. JobListDialog.OnRunNowClick (async void, JobListDialog.cs:1061-1069) awaits the invoker, Form1.RunJobNowAsync awaits _jobExecutionService.RunNowAsync directly (Form1.cs:15319) — no Task.Run anywhere. RunNowAsync therefore runs synchronously on the UI thread through TryStartJob (a jobs.json + .bak disk write, Services/JobExecutionService.cs:768-774) and the whole prefix of ExecuteJobCoreAsync up to the first real await at sshService.ExecutePresetAsync (687): ResolveCredentials (592-645 — a Vault HTTP call for Vault-mode jobs) and BuildHostConnections (487-544), which for every host row carrying a vault_path calls VaultCredentialProvider.TryGetPassword — a sync-over-async network call (Services/Vault/VaultCredentialProvider.cs:48-49) — sequentially, one row at a time. VaultService has a 300s TTL cache (Services/Vault/VaultService.cs:109-143, 1065), so repeated identical paths are cheap once warm, but a fleet with distinct per-host vault paths pays N cold sequential round-trips on the UI thread: 100 hosts at 100ms RTT freezes the window for ~10 seconds with no feedback. The same sequential resolution also delays scheduled runs (off the UI thread) while holding a concurrency slot.
recommendation: Cheapest fix: in RunNowAsync (or Form1.RunJobNowAsync), move the execution onto the thread pool — e.g. await Task.Run(() => ExecuteTrackedJobAsync(job, isRunNow: true)) — so the UI thread returns immediately after the already-running check. Follow-up: make BuildHostConnections resolve distinct vault paths concurrently with a small parallelism cap (the VaultService cache already deduplicates identical paths), which also shortens scheduled-run startup for large fleets.
user_benefit: Clicking Run Now on a Vault-backed fleet no longer freezes the app for the duration of N sequential network calls; the job appears as Running instantly and the window stays responsive.

evidence.note: async void click handler awaits straight into the service on the UI thread
Form1 invoker awaits RunNowAsync directly, no Task.Run
synchronous prefix: TryStartJob disk write, ResolveCredentials, per-row sequential Vault lookups before first await
